item_text: The implemented features match the documented requirements/proposal scope.
Core computations (grading formula, GWA, forecasting features/label) are correctly and verifiably implemented (e.g. the hand-verified test cases in grading/tests.py).
No functionality is missing that a grading-and-forecasting system of this scope should have.
Database queries are reasonably optimized (no obvious N+1 patterns) for the heaviest pages.
Response times stay well under 2 seconds under realistic data volume (see docs/PERFORMANCE.md).
Resource usage (DB connections, memory) is reasonable for the deployment target.
The system runs correctly across modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge).
The system does not conflict with other services on the same deployment (e.g. shares a Postgres instance safely, doesn't hard-code ports/paths that would collide).
Data interchange (Excel import/export, PDF generation) is correct and round-trips cleanly.
The UI follows consistent, predictable patterns across pages (shared CRUD, shared modal, shared table conventions).
Accessibility basics (labels, contrast, keyboard navigation, landmark roles) are present — see docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md.
The information architecture (sidebar, role-based menus) is logical for each role.
The test suite is comprehensive and the measured coverage (see docs/TEST_REPORT.md) is adequate for the code's risk level.
Error handling is graceful — a failure in one subsystem (e.g. forecasting) does not break unrelated pages.
The backup/restore tooling (backup_db/restore_db) is correct and usable.
Authentication and session handling (password hashing, lockout, session expiry) follow reasonable security practice.
Authorization is enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI (role-based + object-level checks).
Sensitive data (passwords, personal data used in forecasting) is handled appropriately (masked identifiers, no plaintext secrets in logs).
Production settings (config/settings/prod.py) enforce secure defaults (HTTPS gating, secret key validation, security headers).
The codebase is modular (clear app boundaries) with minimal unnecessary coupling.
Business logic lives in testable service functions, not scattered across views/templates.
The code and CLAUDE.md documentation are sufficient for a new developer to understand and extend the system.
The test suite would catch a regression if a future change broke existing behavior.
The application can be deployed to a different environment (Ubuntu/Gunicorn/Nginx or Windows/Waitress/NSSM) using the documented steps without code changes.
Configuration (secrets, hosts, feature flags) is externalized via environment variables, not hard-coded.
The system has no unnecessary dependency on a specific OS or hosting provider.
